affiliations.date_precision: The draft-registration card names the employer on February 15, 1942; the biographical chronology places New York electronics-company work before Army induction on November 27, 1942. The exact employment start and end dates are not stated.
affiliations.research_notes: The official image-backed draft-registration record names Nelson Elec Laboratory. Julia Henke's independently sourced chronology says Baronowitz worked for a New York electronics company before Army induction. The evidence supports the last civilian employer before service, not an immediate pre-OSS employer.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Werner Baronowitz is high-confidence matched to the German-born New York electronics worker inducted into the United States Army in 1942.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Werner wurde am 15. April 1904 in Repzin geboren.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The rare exact name, birth details, New York chronology, and Army service recur across an image-backed official draft record and a cited historical biography, aligning with the indexed Pfc.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from the exact rare name, identical birth date and place in two independent sources, New York residence and employment, Army induction, and compatible enlisted index context. Neither reviewed source explicitly names OSS or Box 38.
claims.temporal_assessment: The sources establish New York employment in February 1942, Army induction in November 1942, and Army service through July 1945; the precise OSS interval remains unresolved.
claims.match_notes: The private Army identifier is not reproduced publicly. The match remains high confidence rather than confirmed pending personnel-file or direct OSS-document comparison.
